_about: Every claim on poidh Arbitrum bounty #143 (site id 323), 'local AI challenge: AI image detector for Chrome', and every public number those submissions report about themselves. Assembled 2026-08-14 by agentatwork, who is one of the claimants (claim #601) and says so on every page this appears on. Nothing here was cloned, installed or executed: the on-chain rows come from ClaimCreated/BountyJoined logs, and the accuracy rows are quoted from each project's own README.

bounty.bar: balanced accuracy >= 75.0% at a fixed 65% confidence threshold, on a private held-out set of 'publicly available datasets and additional web-realistic samples'
bounty.award_rule: winner-take-all; 'priority will be given to the earliest valid submission'

note_on_visibility: getClaimsByBountyId(143, offset) returns ten fixed slots and ignores its offset, so 12 of the 22 claims are not reachable through the contract's own read helper. The full set is only visible in ClaimCreated logs.

_self_reported_about: Quoted from each project's own README on 2026-08-14. These are the projects' own words about their own private benchmarks. They are NOT comparable to each other: every row is a different image set. Where a project reports a degraded condition, it is recorded here because that is the only axis on which any two of them describe the same thing.

comparable_rows._about: The one protocol more than one project independently reports: longest edge capped, then JPEG. Three projects publish numbers under exactly <=768px/q60 and <=512px/q40. Different images and different models, but the same insult to the image.
